text:
A focused cycle at the desk began with your letter, and we are sorry to learn that your recent journey with Aurelia Skyways and your companion animal did not meet the standard of care you expected. You reported that the handling of your pet, the communication at acceptance, and the support during transfer felt disorganized and left you uncertain about safety.

We treat that concern as serious. Safety takes priority over speed in every journey. When a complaint reaches the Companion Animal Travel Desk, it is reviewed with the same urgency we apply to live-animal handling, because even a brief lapse can create avoidable stress for both traveler and animal. The safety coordinator has been asked to examine the chain of events, the condition checks, and the handoff points used on your trip. That review is focused on prevention, not blame, and it will be used to correct weak points before they affect another traveler.

You should have received clearer guidance at each step. Travel guidance is concise, kind, and actionable. We are reinforcing that standard with front-line staff so that owners receive plain instructions on crate placement, document checks, and transfer support without delay or confusion. We are also reminding teams that if an issue is seen, it must be reported at once and handled before the journey continues.

If the concern involved a delay in care, missed reassurance, or a lack of visible oversight, that is not acceptable to us. A companion animal should never be treated as an afterthought. The desk is reviewing whether the procedure was followed correctly and whether additional checks are needed before release, loading, or onward movement.

We regret the distress this caused you and your pet. Please accept our apology and our commitment to tighter oversight on future travel. If you choose to travel again with Aurelia Skyways, the Companion Animal Travel Desk will work to provide steadier support and clearer handling from start to finish. Companion Animal Travel Desk
